column1: # Allowlist of the test scan gate (issue 266, A277): every wait candidate of `test-scan --kind wait` that must stay in proofline's own tests. CI runs
# `node control-plane/agents/scripts/proofline-core.mjs cli test-scan --kind wait --allowlist tests/ci/test-scan-allowlist.tsv tests` and fails on an open candidate or a stale entry.
# <path glob><TAB><pattern><TAB><reason>   (one entry per line, sorted by path then pattern; a reason says why nothing waits for a duration or why no event exists)

column3: False positive: the helper that calls mock.timers.enable for the timeout function; it holds the timers of the code under test and the tests fire them with tick, nothing waits for a duration

False positive: heldClock replaces globalThis.setTimeout by a clock that only stores the limit and grace callbacks; the test fires them when the event they are about is true, nothing waits for a duration

Real 20 ms poll between checks of state a separate process writes (the shell-script fake runtimes of dispatch-lib.mjs: pid files, markers, ledger lines, a process that has ended); the fakes cannot tell the test. To remove it the fakes report over a socket (event-lib.mjs) and a process gone becomes the close of its connection. Used only by dispatch.test.mjs and dispatch-watchdog.test.mjs

The sleepSync of the manual end-to-end harness (drives the real claude/codex CLI, NOT run by CI): its only caller is the bounded 5 s wait in cleanup() for the lead process group to exit after SIGTERM, before rm; the group is a real OS process tree started through a CLI with no event the harness can wait on (ps stat is what it polls).

tests/e2e/run.mjs only (the manual harness that runs a scenario with a real model; NOT run by CI; the helper tests tests/e2e/*.test.mjs are a different file and are not covered): one-second supervision tick of its loop; a real session cannot run on a fake clock

tests/e2e/run.mjs only (the manual harness that runs a scenario with a real model; NOT run by CI; the helper tests tests/e2e/*.test.mjs are a different file and are not covered): supervision tick that races the exit event of the lead process, so a normal exit does not wait for it

The call of the sleepSync helper in cleanup() of the manual end-to-end harness (NOT run by CI): bounded 100 ms steps, at most 50, while the real lead process group ends after SIGTERM so that rm never races a live process; no event exists for a process tree started by a vendor CLI.

watchdog of the runGroup helper: cleared on close, fires only when the command hangs and then kills its process group and fails the run; a run that ends normally never waits for it. Removal would need an injected clock in the helper and no test depends on the expiry here
source text of a child process the test spawns: setImmediate defers the exit by one event-loop turn, it is not a duration and nothing sleeps
source text of a child process the test spawns: a never-firing keepalive (2^30 ms) that holds the child open until the test sends it a signal; the test waits for the exit event, not for the interval

tests/real-session/smoke.mjs only (the manual smoke harness that calls the real claude CLI; NOT run by CI; tests/real-session/*.test.mjs helper tests are other files and are not covered): sleep helper definition and per-step watchdog (kills the process group on expiry)

tests/real-session/smoke.mjs only (the manual smoke harness that calls the real claude CLI; NOT run by CI; tests/real-session/*.test.mjs helper tests are other files and are not covered): two real 2 s sleeps so the next hook message has a later whole-second timestamp than the question; the product stamps messages in whole seconds and has no clock seam: a KNOWN OPEN SEAM, accepted limit (lead decision)
the hand clock of the process-group test: its setTimeout method only stores the callback and fires on advance(); it waits for nothing (A277)
